nodes.name: Etching to form NiFe-LDH
nodes.procedure: Weigh 1.8 g of FeCl3·6H2O dissolved in 20 mL of deionized water and 0.2 g of Na2S2O3 dissolved in 10 mL of deionized water, and turn on the electromagnetic stirring to make them form homogeneous solutions respectively. The treated NF was put into the FeCl3 solution, immediately followed by pouring the Na2S2O3 solution into it and starting the timing, and it was removed after 60 s. It was labeled as Ni0@NiFe-LDH/NF.

nodes.name: Electrodeposition of Ni (9 min)
nodes.procedure: 3 g of NiCl2·6H2O and 0.2 g of CH3COONa were weighed and dissolved in 30 mL of deionized water, and prepared as the electrodeposition solution. The cathodic deposition method was used to obtain Ni9@NiFe-LDH/NF by electrodeposition at a current of 100 mA for 9 min.

nodes.name: Pt/C coating on NF
nodes.procedure: Disperse a mixture of commercial Pt/C powder (8 mg), carbon black (1.5 mg), and 5 μL of Nafion solution (0.5 wt%) in 1000 μL of ethanol solution. The above solution was ultrasonically dried and then coated on the treated nickel foam, and the Pt/C/NF catalysts was successfully prepared. Test after air-drying.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni0@NiFe-LDH/NF shows nanoflake-like structures; Ni3@NiFe-LDH/NF and Ni9@NiFe-LDH/NF show high density nickel nanoparticles aggregating into globular flower-like morphology with increased compactness.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Following corrosion treatment with ferric ions, the SEM image of the catalyst (Fig. 2a-b) reveals the formation of numerous nanoflake-like structures... Upon further deposition of nickel ions by electrodeposition, the SEM image of the NiFe-LDH/NF catalyst shows a high density of nickel nanoparticles, which aggregate into a globular, flower-like morphology (Fig. 2cf).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni9@NiFe-LDH/NF shows lamellar structure at 200 nm and 100 nm scales.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM image (Fig. 2g-h) of the Ni₉@NiFe-LDH/NF catalyst further corroborates the lamellar structure observed in the SEM images.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni9@NiFe-LDH/NF shows uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, O, and S elements across the catalyst surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) analysis (Fig. 2i) reveals the uniform distribution of Ni, Fe, O, and S elements across the catalyst surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: All catalysts show Ni crystalline facets from nickel foam substrate at 44.59°, 51.91°, and 76.80°; Ni3@NiFe-LDH/NF and Ni9@NiFe-LDH/NF show higher diffraction intensities than Ni0@NiFe-LDH/NF.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The diffraction patterns revealed distinct peaks at 44.59°, 51.91°, and 76.80°, corresponding to the Ni crystalline facets of the nickel foam substrate... Notably, the diffraction intensities of the Ni3@NiFe-LDH/NF and Ni₉@NiFe-LDH/NF catalysts were higher compared to those of the Ni₀@NiFe-LDH/NF catalyst.

nodes.evidence_snippet: Raman spectroscopy was employed... the prominent peak at 528.4 cm⁻¹ corresponds to the characteristic Ni-O stretching vibration, indicating that NiO is the predominant nickel species present on the catalyst surface.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni9@NiFe-LDH/NF shows Cdl = 16.66 mF cm⁻² (non-Faradaic region for HER ECSA estimation), highest among catalysts; Ni3@NiFe-LDH/NF: 6.73 mF cm⁻²; Ni0@NiFe-LDH/NF: 2.69 mF cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: From the analysis of the CV curves, we calculated the capacitive double-layer capacitance (Cdl) values for each catalyst. Ni₉@NiFe-LDH/NF demonstrated the highest Cdl value of 16.66 mF cm⁻², compared to 2.69 mF cm⁻² for Ni₀@NiFe-LDH/NF and 6.73 mF cm⁻² for Ni₃@NiFe-LDH/NF (Fig. 4e).
